messages:
Maya K.: FYI we got MeterMint's renewal quote. Their rep proposes a 'commit-split' — 70% committed credits, 30% pay-as-you-go. Need input on how this maps to our burst needs and TCO. Attaching their sample math.

Ashish P.: can you paste the numbers? I want to see per-token/embedding rates and how overage is priced.

Maya K.: Sure — excerpt below.
```
Plan A (12mo): commit 700k tokens/mo @ $0.0004/token = $280/mo committed
Overage: $0.0006/token
Burst up to 2x commit free for 48 hrs/month
Setup fee: $5k
```

Carl R.: Hmm per-token looks fine but 700k/mo seems low for infra. What's embed pricing? Also what's their definition of 'token' for billing? Requesting model usage mapping.

Liz H.: MeterMint said embeddings billed per 1k vectors @ $0.15 committed, $0.25 overage. Also they apply a 10% uplift on estimated usage when calculating commit.

Ashish P.: Two concerns: 1) uplift skews commit so we may overcommit and waste spend. 2) burst allowance rolling monthly vs calendar month matters for engineering. Ask legal for termination window.

Maya K.: I asked rep these questions, they replied:
> The 10% uplift is standard; we can negotiate waiver if you provide 3-month usage history and agree to 6mo commit.
> Burst resets monthly (calendar).
> We can cap overage at 2x committed for enterprise plan.

They offered a 6mo pilot pricing where the uplift drops to 3%.

Carl R.: Can someone run a simple model: take our last 6mo tokens and simulate commit at 90th percentile vs 80th. I can run if you drop the numbers.

Liz H.: I'll export usage. Maya — can you confirm what reporting window rep needs? 3 months or 6 months?

Maya K.: They asked for 3 months to waive uplift, but 6 months for pilot. I'll drop the CSV here in a sec.

Procurement Bot: File uploaded: usage_2025-09_to_2025-11.csv (3.2 MB)

Ashish P.: After we have the sim, we should ask for a seat-equivalent comparison — i.e., what a seat-based price would look like for our team with same usage. MeterMint didn't initially provide seat pricing.

Carl R.: Agreed. Also ask for a clause: predictable per-token rate if we pin to a model family (e.g., Llama-2-70B-quant). Otherwise they could change token definition.

Maya K.: Good point. I'll request: 1) model-family anchoring 2) calendar-month burst clarification 3) overage cap language 4) seat vs usage comparison

Anyone want to add items before I reply to rep?

Liz H.: Add SLA for billing disputes — 45-day dispute window and monthly reconciliations.

Ashish P.: And require sample invoice format. Past vendor invoices lacked per-route breakdown which we need for cost attribution.

Carl R.: Thx. With these asks, sounds negotiable. If they hold on uplift, consider starting with 3mo pilot + 6mo commitment.

Maya K.: Great — I'll send a follow-up by EOD. Leaving here for now :thumbsup:
